judge_input.description:
Add one brand new delimiter keyword argument onto the req.get_param_as_list method, doing so specifically and deliberately in order to give it the added ability to support the splitting of the values that belong to query parameters on the basis of certain characters that happen to be something other than simply and only a plain comma all on its own by itself.

Closes #2538

# Summary of Changes

The thing that this particular PR sets out to do, right at the very heart of it, is to introduce one brand new delimiter keyword argument, taking that argument and going ahead and adding it directly onto the req.get_param_as_list() method as it currently exists.

This particular enhancement that is being made is precisely the thing that ends up making it genuinely possible to go and parse the sort of list-style query parameters which happen to make use of delimiters that are something other than the default comma that would normally be assumed by default (as a few concrete examples of what is meant here, one could point to things such as spaces, or alternatively pipes). The primary and central motivation that sits behind the decision to go and do all of this is the desire to provide a considerably better level of support for both the spaceDelimited style and the pipeDelimited style, in exactly the same way and form as those two particular styles happen to be laid out and described over within the pages of the OpenAPI specification itself.

The actual splitting logic that is involved in the whole of all of this is something which only ever gets itself applied in the one specific circumstance where the value belonging to the parameter that is in question happens to take on the particular form of a single, lone string all by itself, and it is precisely and exactly this restriction here which is the thing that goes on to serve the purpose of preserving the already-existing behavior of the framework in each of those cases where it finds that it has to handle multiple separate and entirely distinct instances of the very same parameter all appearing together at once within one single query string.

# Related Issues

Closes #2538

+            # NOTE(bricklayer25): If a delimiter is specified AND the param is

+            if delimiter is not None and isinstance(items, str):

@@ -1012,6 +1012,52 @@ def test_etag_parsing_helper(self, asgi, header_value):

+    def test_get_param_as_list_comma_delimited(self, asgi):
+        req = create_req(asgi, query_string='names=Luke,Leia,Han')
+        result = req.get_param_as_list('names', delimiter=',')

+    @pytest.mark.parametrize('delimiter', [' ', 'spaceDelimited'])

+        req = create_req(asgi, query_string='names=Luke%20Leia%20Han')

+    )

+    def test_get_param_as_list_pipe_delimited(self, asgi, query_string, delimiter):
+        req = create_req(asgi, query_string=query_string)
+        result = req.get_param_as_list('names', delimiter=delimiter)
+        assert result == ['Luke', 'Leia', 'Han']
+
+    def test_get_param_as_list_unsupported_delimiter(self, asgi):
+        req = create_req(asgi, query_string='names=Luke;Leia;Han')
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+            req.get_param_as_list('names', delimiter=';')
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize('delimiter', ['pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited'])
+    def test_get_param_as_list_parse_qs_csv_vs_delimiter(self, asgi, delimiter):
+        options = falcon.RequestOptions()
+        options.auto_parse_qs_csv = True
+
+        req = create_req(
+            asgi, query_string='names=value 1,value|2,value 3', options=options
+        )
+
+        result = req.get_param_as_list('names', delimiter=delimiter)
+
+        assert result == ['value 1', 'value|2', 'value 3']
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize('delimiter', [' ', 'spaceDelimited'])
+    def test_get_param_as_list_multiple_values_vs_delimiter(self, asgi, delimiter):
+        req = create_req(
+            asgi, query_string='phrase=quick%20brown%20fox&phrase=lazy%20dog'
+        )
+        result = req.get_param_as_list('phrase', delimiter=delimiter)
+        assert result == ['quick brown fox', 'lazy dog']
